page: Amazon Web Services m7g.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by custom 64-core AWS Graviton processors using the ARM64 architecture. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated physical cores with single-thread execution operating at 2.6 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local NVMe SSD storage, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core execution and software compilation tasks using Clang, as well as in Passmark memory metrics. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 6193.1 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and up to 253.34 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Multi-core stress-ng tests and Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong throughput, while single-core performance remains in the average tier.

Given its ARM-based architecture and high physical core density, the m7g.16xlarge offers a resource-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads. It is highly suited for application servers, software compilation pipelines, static web serving, and database operations like Redis. However, the lack of local storage and specialized GPU hardware makes it less suitable for heavy local disk-I/O tasks or large-scale deep learning training.
